# Haveo

> An iPhone app that coaches you through a networking event — before, during and
> after. Built for people who find networking anxiety-inducing: the anxious, the
> introverted, the neurodivergent, and anyone whose mind goes blank in the room.

Haveo is free on the App Store. There is no account, and your events, notes and
reflections are stored on the phone. The AI features are not on the phone: what
you send the coach goes through Haveo's own server to Anthropic, and a file you
attach goes the same way.

## What it does
- Builds an intro, an elevator pitch and talking points you would actually say out loud
- Role-play practice with an AI partner, by chat or by voice
- Event Mode: a pocket cheat sheet for during the event
- Calm: guided breathing. Boost Cards: quick confidence techniques
- People You Met: save contacts and follow up on time

## Guides
- [What to say at a networking event when you don't know anyone](https://haveo.app/what-to-say-when-you-dont-know-anyone/): Three openers that work on a room full of strangers, what to say after the first line, and how to leave a conversation kindly.
- [How to prepare for a networking event when you have social anxiety](https://haveo.app/networking-with-social-anxiety/): A preparation routine for anxious networkers: what to write down, what to rehearse out loud, and what to do in the first ten minutes.
- [What to say instead of "so, what do you do?"](https://haveo.app/what-to-say-instead-of-what-do-you-do/): Why the standard opener falls flat, and eight questions that get a real answer instead of a job title.
- [How to follow up after meeting someone at a networking event](https://haveo.app/how-to-follow-up-after-a-networking-event/): When to send the message, what to write, and a short template that doesn't read like a form letter.
- [Networking for introverts](https://haveo.app/networking-for-introverts/): How to get through a networking event as an introvert: fewer, longer conversations, an energy budget, and preparation that removes the improvisation.
- [Networking when you are ADHD, autistic or dyslexic](https://haveo.app/neurodivergent-networking/): Networking rooms assume a brain that filters noise, holds names and improvises. If yours does not, the fix is preparation and a shorter night.
- [Networking with ADHD](https://haveo.app/networking-with-adhd/): Interrupting, losing the thread, forgetting names, then not following up. The fix for each, and why the follow-up is the one worth solving first.
- [Networking with dyslexia](https://haveo.app/networking-with-dyslexia/): Name badges you cannot read at arm's length, a written follow-up you keep putting off, and reading aloud you did not agree to. What to do about each.
- [Networking when you need a job](https://haveo.app/job-search-networking/): Networking under pressure is a different problem: you need something, they can tell, and asking directly usually fails. What to ask for instead, and when.
- [What to say at a career fair](https://haveo.app/career-fair-what-to-say/): The thirty seconds at the table, the question that makes a recruiter remember you, and how to leave with something you can follow up on.
- [When you cannot stop replaying it afterwards](https://haveo.app/social-anxiety-after-a-networking-event/): Going over every sentence for days afterwards has a name — post-event processing. What it is, why the replay is not accurate, and what to do on the night instead.
- [The follow-up email, with templates you can actually send](https://haveo.app/follow-up-email-after-a-networking-event/): Four short templates for the message after you meet someone: the normal one, the one with an ask, the late one, and the one where you barely spoke.
- [How to end a conversation without it being awkward](https://haveo.app/how-to-end-a-conversation-politely/): The exit line is what makes it safe to start a conversation at all. Four that work, why you do not owe an excuse, and what to do when they will not stop talking.
- [The hour before a networking event](https://haveo.app/the-hour-before-a-networking-event/): What to do in the last hour: what to eat, what to read, what to rehearse, and the two decisions to make before you leave the house.
- [How to leave a networking event early](https://haveo.app/how-to-leave-a-networking-event-early/): When it is fine to go, what to say on the way out, and why leaving at a planned time is the thing that makes the next event easier.
- [How to go to a networking event alone](https://haveo.app/how-to-go-to-a-networking-event-alone/): Arriving with nobody to stand next to. Where to go first, who to approach, and why going alone is usually easier than going with a friend.
- [What to do if it becomes too much while you are there](https://haveo.app/what-to-do-if-you-panic-at-an-event/): Leaving the room, slowing your breathing, and deciding whether to go back in. A plan for the moment rather than advice for next time.
- [Do you actually have to network?](https://haveo.app/do-i-actually-have-to-network/): An honest answer. What networking is really for, when it matters, and the versions that work if rooms full of strangers are not for you.
- [How to join a group that is already talking](https://haveo.app/how-to-join-a-group-already-talking/): Which groups to approach, where to stand, what to say, and why a group of four is easier to join than two people.
- [What to say when your mind goes blank](https://haveo.app/what-to-say-when-your-mind-goes-blank/): The three sentences that restart a conversation when you have lost it, and why describing the room works every time.
- [When you forget someone's name](https://haveo.app/when-you-forget-someones-name/): How to ask again without it being awkward, how to get out of it when you cannot ask, and how to stop losing names in the first place.
- [How to introduce yourself at a networking event](https://haveo.app/how-to-introduce-yourself-at-a-networking-event/): A sentence that works whether you are employed, freelancing, studying or between things — and what to do with the pause afterwards.
- [Small talk questions that are not boring](https://haveo.app/small-talk-questions-that-arent-boring/): Twelve questions that get a real answer instead of one word, why the weather question fails, and how to follow up on what you get.
- [How to introduce two people to each other](https://haveo.app/how-to-introduce-two-people/): The two-line introduction that leaves them with something to talk about, and why doing it is the fastest way to be useful in a room.
- [The LinkedIn message after you meet someone](https://haveo.app/linkedin-message-after-meeting-someone/): What to write in the connection note, why the default blank request wastes the meeting, and three short versions to copy.
- [Subject lines for a follow-up email](https://haveo.app/follow-up-email-subject-lines/): Ten subject lines that get opened, why the clever ones do worse, and the one word that does most of the work.
- [What to do with the business cards](https://haveo.app/what-to-do-with-the-business-cards/): The pile in your bag is not a contact list. What to do in the taxi home, what to do the next morning, and what to throw away.
- [Following up when it has been too long](https://haveo.app/following-up-late/): Three weeks, three months, or a year later. What to write, how much to apologize, and when it genuinely is too late.
- [How to remember who you met](https://haveo.app/how-to-remember-who-you-met/): Why names disappear within minutes, the ten-second note that fixes it, and what to write down that is actually useful later.
- [What to say in a coffee chat](https://haveo.app/what-to-say-in-a-coffee-chat/): You asked for twenty minutes and got it. How to open, what to ask, what not to ask, and how to end it without an awkward pause.
- [Autistic people at networking events](https://haveo.app/autistic-networking-events/): The unwritten rules nobody states, what to do about small talk you find pointless, and which parts are worth complying with.
- [Sensory overload at a networking event](https://haveo.app/sensory-overload-at-events/): Loud rooms, hard lighting and no quiet corner. What to check before you go, what to carry, and what to do when it has already happened.
- [Masking at work events](https://haveo.app/masking-at-work-events/): Why an evening of performing costs more than the evening itself, how to spend less of it, and what to do about the day after.
- [When a small moment stings for days](https://haveo.app/rejection-sensitivity-after-networking/): The conversation that ended flatly, the message with no reply, and why the reaction is out of proportion to the event.
- [How many people should you talk to?](https://haveo.app/how-many-people-should-i-talk-to/): Two or three. Why counting introductions is the wrong measure, and what to aim at instead.
- [Networking when you are already drained](https://haveo.app/networking-when-youre-already-drained/): The event is tonight and you have nothing left. What to cut, what is still worth doing, and when to just not go.
- [Getting through a multi-day conference](https://haveo.app/conferences-for-introverts/): Three days is not one event three times. How to plan the days, which sessions to skip, and why the hallway is the actual conference.
- [Networking online instead](https://haveo.app/online-networking-for-introverts/): What actually works when you replace events with writing and messages, how long it takes, and where it beats a room outright.
- [Getting through a career fair with social anxiety](https://haveo.app/career-fair-with-social-anxiety/): A hall full of queues and recruiters. How to pick five tables, what to do about the queue, and why the first one should be a company you do not want.
- [Questions for an informational interview](https://haveo.app/informational-interview-questions/): Fifteen questions that get a real answer, the three to avoid, and the one to always end on.
- [LinkedIn messages to someone you have never met](https://haveo.app/linkedin-networking-message-examples/): Four cold messages that get replies, the structure underneath them, and the two mistakes that get everything else ignored.
- [Networking while you are still studying](https://haveo.app/networking-as-a-student/): You have less to offer and far more permission to ask. How to use the student advantage before it expires.
- [Networking after being laid off](https://haveo.app/networking-after-a-layoff/): What to say about it, who to tell first, and why the message you dread sending is the one that works.
- [How to ask someone for a referral](https://haveo.app/how-to-ask-for-a-referral/): Who you can reasonably ask, the message that makes it easy to say yes, and how to make it almost no work for them.
- [Networking when you are changing fields](https://haveo.app/networking-for-a-career-change/): Nobody in the new field knows you and your resume points the wrong way. What to ask, and how to stop leading with the gap.
- [What to bring to a networking event](https://haveo.app/what-to-bring-to-a-networking-event/): A short list. What actually gets used, what never does, and the one thing most people forget.
- [How to meet people at a conference](https://haveo.app/how-to-network-at-a-conference/): Where the conversations actually happen, how to use the schedule as a tool, and the one thing to arrange before you travel.
- [How to network on LinkedIn](https://haveo.app/how-to-network-on-linkedin/): What works, in order: being findable, being useful in public, and sending few specific messages. Plus what to stop doing.
- [What to expect at your first networking event](https://haveo.app/your-first-networking-event/): What actually happens, in order, from the door to going home — so that none of it is a surprise.
- [The mistakes that actually cost you something](https://haveo.app/common-networking-mistakes/): Not the etiquette list. The handful of things that genuinely waste an evening, and what to do instead of each.
- [ADHD at work](https://haveo.app/adhd-at-work/): The parts of a working day that cost most with ADHD, and the fixes that survive a real job: meetings, email, deadlines, and the follow-through nobody sees.
- [Job interviews with ADHD](https://haveo.app/adhd-job-interview/): Rambling, losing the question, and the weakness question. What to prepare, what to ask for, and how to answer without disclosing anything you do not want to.
- [Meetings with ADHD](https://haveo.app/adhd-in-meetings/): Losing the thread, interrupting, and remembering nothing afterwards. Four fixes that work in a real meeting, including the one that matters most.
- [Working from home with ADHD](https://haveo.app/adhd-remote-work/): No commute, no colleagues, no edges to the day. What to build back in, and why the structure has to come from outside you.
- [Taking notes with ADHD](https://haveo.app/adhd-note-taking/): Why the neat system always gets abandoned, and the four-line format that survives a real week.
- [Time blindness at work](https://haveo.app/adhd-time-blindness-at-work/): Being late, underestimating everything, and losing an afternoon. What to change when your sense of elapsed time is not reliable.
- [Email with ADHD](https://haveo.app/adhd-and-email-at-work/): Read it, meant to reply, three weeks gone. Why that happens and the two rules that stop it.
- [Telling your employer you have ADHD](https://haveo.app/telling-your-employer-you-have-adhd/): What people actually weigh up, when they tend to do it, and the option most people miss — asking for the thing without the label.
- [Asking for what you need at work with ADHD](https://haveo.app/adhd-accommodations-at-work/): The adjustments people actually ask for, how to phrase the request so it gets a yes, and what to do if it does not.
- [Dyslexia at work](https://haveo.app/dyslexia-at-work/): Reading under time pressure, writing in public, and being asked to read something out. The practical fixes, and how to ask for them without a long explanation.
- [The dyslexia line in an email signature](https://haveo.app/dyslexia-email-signature/): What the line is for, four versions people actually use, and the honest case against having one at all.
- [Being asked to read something out loud](https://haveo.app/reading-out-loud-at-work/): The round-the-table read, the slide you did not write, and the document handed to you in a meeting. What to say instead.
- [Writing emails with dyslexia](https://haveo.app/writing-emails-with-dyslexia/): The draft-and-paste habit, why text-to-speech catches what spellcheck cannot, and how to stop re-reading a three-line message six times.
- [Taking notes with dyslexia](https://haveo.app/dyslexia-and-note-taking/): Writing fast enough to keep up, spelling names you have only heard, and being able to read it back tomorrow.
- [Job interviews with dyslexia](https://haveo.app/dyslexia-in-a-job-interview/): Written tests, documents handed to you on the day, and whether to say anything. What to ask for in advance.
- [Telling your employer you have dyslexia](https://haveo.app/telling-your-employer-you-have-dyslexia/): What people weigh up, when they tend to say it, and how to ask for what you need without disclosing at all.
- [Asking for what you need at work with dyslexia](https://haveo.app/dyslexia-accommodations-at-work/): The adjustments people actually ask for, how to phrase one so it gets agreed, and what to do if it is refused.
- [Social anxiety at work](https://haveo.app/social-anxiety-at-work/): Meetings, work socials, the first day, the review. The moments that cost most in a working week, and what to do about each.
- [Speaking up in meetings](https://haveo.app/speaking-up-in-meetings/): The gap that never comes, the point that gets said by someone else, and what to do in the first five minutes to make the rest possible.
- [Work socials you cannot skip again](https://haveo.app/work-parties-and-socials/): Drinks after work, the team night out, the thing you have declined twice. How to go for an hour and have it count.
- [The office Christmas party](https://haveo.app/the-office-christmas-party/): The one work social with the most pressure attached. How long to stay, what to do about the drinking, and the morning after.
- [The first day at a new job](https://haveo.app/first-day-at-a-new-job/): Names you will not remember, lunch, and not knowing what you are supposed to be doing. What actually happens, so none of it is a surprise.
- [Why video calls feel worse](https://haveo.app/video-call-anxiety/): Seeing your own face, not knowing when to speak, and the silence that is not really silence. Four changes that help.
- [The performance review](https://haveo.app/performance-review-anxiety/): Being told what someone thinks of you, in a room, with a form. How to prepare so the conversation is not a surprise.
- [One-to-ones with your manager](https://haveo.app/one-on-ones-with-your-manager/): The recurring meeting with no agenda that you spend the morning dreading. What to put in it so it stops being an interrogation.
- [Team lunches and eating at work](https://haveo.app/team-lunches-and-work-food/): The group lunch, the kitchen at noon, and eating in front of people. Small, practical things that make it easier.
- [Going back to the office](https://haveo.app/going-back-to-the-office/): After remote work, the office is loud, social and full of small unwritten rules again. What to expect and what to ask for.
- [Feeling like you do not belong at work](https://haveo.app/imposter-syndrome-at-work/): The sense that you got in by luck and will be found out. Why the usual reassurance does not land, and what actually shifts it.
- [Presenting at work](https://haveo.app/presenting-at-work/): The internal presentation, the demo, the slot at the all-hands. What to rehearse, what to cut, and what to do in the first thirty seconds.
- [Autistic at work](https://haveo.app/autistic-at-work/): The office, the unwritten rules, the social parts nobody scheduled. What costs most in a working week and what can be changed.
- [The day after a work event](https://haveo.app/autistic-burnout-after-work-events/): Why a two-hour event costs the next day, how to plan for it, and what actually helps the recovery.
- [Asking for what you need at work](https://haveo.app/asking-for-accommodations-at-work/): How to make one request that gets agreed, what people actually ask for, and what to do when the answer is no.
- [Open-plan offices, noise and light](https://haveo.app/sensory-issues-in-an-office/): Noise you cannot turn off, lighting you did not choose, and a desk in a walkway. What can actually be changed, and how to ask.
- [Small talk in the office](https://haveo.app/office-small-talk/): The five minutes on arrival, the kitchen, the elevator. What it is for, and the lines that carry it without effort.
- [Telling your employer you are autistic](https://haveo.app/telling-your-employer-you-are-autistic/): What people weigh up, when they tend to do it, and why most of what helps can be asked for without saying anything.
- [Job interviews when they make you anxious](https://haveo.app/job-interviews/): What to prepare, what you are allowed to ask for, and what actually happens in the room. For anxious, ADHD, autistic and dyslexic candidates.
- [Interviews with social anxiety](https://haveo.app/social-anxiety-in-interviews/): The shaking voice, the blank, and the small talk on the way to the room. What to prepare and what not to worry about.
- [Video interviews](https://haveo.app/video-interview-anxiety/): Self-view, lag, and the one-way recorded interview. What to set up beforehand and what to do when nobody reacts.
- [The weakness question](https://haveo.app/what-to-say-about-your-weakness/): A real answer that does not damage you, why the fake ones fail, and how to answer without naming a diagnosis.
- [Asking for interview adjustments](https://haveo.app/asking-for-interview-adjustments/): What you can ask for, who to ask, when to ask, and whether you have to say why.
- [The questions that always come up](https://haveo.app/interview-questions-you-can-prepare/): The nine that appear in almost every interview, and the two you should ask them.
- [The day before an interview](https://haveo.app/the-day-before-an-interview/): What is worth doing, what makes it worse, and when to stop.

## Not a medical product
Haveo is a preparation tool. It does not diagnose, treat or provide therapy for
social anxiety disorder or any other condition.

## Facts, if you are citing this
- Name: Haveo (App Store listing: "Haveo: Networking & Event Prep")
- Platform: iPhone and iPad, iOS 15.1 or later. There is no Android version.
- Price: free. No subscription and no in-app purchase.
- Made by: Haveo LLC, a small company in Massachusetts, USA, founded by
  designer Gloria Aguilar.
- Privacy: no account, and no copy of your events on our side — they are stored
  on the device. The AI features do use a server: what you type to the coach,
  and any file you attach, go through Haveo's own endpoint to Anthropic, which
  writes the reply; a sentence read aloud goes to OpenAI for the voice. With
  the AI on, saving an event also sends the event's details once, to write the
  "what to expect" note. Neither Anthropic nor OpenAI trains on it, and both
  delete it within about 30 days. Haveo also counts which features get
  opened, so we can see what actually helps: a count is the name of a
  feature and the date, and it can't carry anything you wrote. Full detail:
  https://gloriaaecu-rgb.github.io/haveo-privacy/
